objective.name: wrapper.stop
objective.description: Stop a named wrapper in the current context. Sends a stop signal to the wrapper process and force-kills after timeout if still running.

#root.role: Resolve the named wrapper, emit a stop signal to the wrapper transport, schedule a force-kill after StopTimeoutMs, and emit a response.

name._comment: Required. Name of the wrapper to stop.

payload._comment: Empty payload. The stop signal has been sent. The wrapper process may still be running until stop_timeout_ms elapses.

effects.wrapper_runtime: The wrapper process receives a stop signal. State is marked ProcStopping. Force-kill may follow after StopTimeoutMs.

transformation_contract.morphing: A stop request becomes a stopping or stopped wrapper process.
invariants: params.name must refer to a wrapper declared in execution config.
The handler runs asynchronously — it does not block the execution inbox.
Stop is best-effort: a graceful stop signal is sent, and a force-kill is scheduled after the wrapper's configured stop timeout if the process has not exited.
success: Emits an OK response with empty payload after the stop signal is dispatched.
failure: Emits an error response when the wrapper name is missing or not configured.
